prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: the two frames of the sky marker beam: one very tall thin vertical lance of white light edged in violet.

Design identity to keep exactly — the beam is a weapon lance, not scenery: a straight vertical shaft of pure white light (#fff0c0-white core line) inside a violet energy halo (#a058e8 with #4a1a8a outer pixels), edges stepped by pixels, perfectly straight sides, no fade into the background, no clouds, no explosion.

Rebuild it as a sprite sheet under this strict contract:
- On a CONTINUOUS flat pure bright green chroma-key background, exactly hex #51e018, identical solid colour in every background pixel: no gradient, no vignette, no shadow, no floor plane, no panel, no second green shade.
- EXACTLY 2 square cells laid out as 2 ROWS OF 1 (1-column by 2-row) — every cell holding exactly ONE subject; a missing, empty or merged cell ruins the entire sheet.
- Cells in reading order (left-right, then top-bottom):
  cell 1 = the sky-lance beam, FULL frame — a single slender VERTICAL column of light standing top-to-bottom through the whole cell height, white-hot core flanked by a violet halo, hard pixel edges The subject lies within aspect 0.08:1 to 0.26:1, the same style, palette and cell-centred placement as the other cells — only the named subject changes.
  cell 2 = the sky-lance beam, FADED frame — the SAME column half as wide, darker core, the violet halo mostly gone The subject lies within aspect 0.07:1 to 0.22:1, the same style, palette and cell-centred placement as the other cells — only the named subject changes.
- The sheet canvas measures EXACTLY 288×576 px. Produce EXACTLY 2 subject cells — no more, no fewer — and nothing else on the sheet.
- Each subject sits well inside its cell with at least 8 px of unbroken flat #51e018 around it and clean flat gutters between cells: no subject may touch or cross a cell edge; keep every subject within the inner 75% of its cell.
- CENTRING AND SIZE: every subject sits at the exact centre of its cell and stays small — at least one quarter of the cell width is empty flat key to its left AND right, and the same above and below; a subject leaning on, touching or crossing a cell border ruins the whole sheet.
- NO guide lines, NO cell borders, NO divider lines, NO frames, NO text, NO labels, NO numbers anywhere on the sheet — the cell names above are ordering instructions and must NEVER be drawn.
- Style: the finest retro pixel art for its native resolution — crisp hard-edged square pixels, chunky bold forms, a rich four-to-six step shading ramp lit from the top-left with careful inner detail and real material texture, clean saturated colours, a 1-px near-black outline on every silhouette edge, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no smooth gradients.
- ORIENTATION LAW: each beam is a narrow vertical pillar — many times TALLER than wide (about 15 times taller than wide), spanning at least 80% of its cell height while taking only a tenth of its width. A horizontal bar or a thick column ruins the sheet. It still may not touch the cell edge: leave flat #51e018 all around. The two lances share the same vertical centre line and the same height.
negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, letters, labels, numbers, cell borders, guide lines, grid lines, watermark, signature, blurry, anti-aliasing, smooth gradient background, scenery, stars, cast shadow, drop shadow, multiple subjects per cell, empty cell, cropped subject, subject touching edge
label: b-beam
